# The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild

[Setup](setup_en.md) · [In the game](ingame_en.md) · **Options** · [Hosting](hosting_en.md) ·
[Trackers](poptracker_en.md) · [Mods](mods_en.md) · [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting_en.md)

## What does randomization do to this game?

The rewards of the game's milestones become Archipelago locations: clearing a shrine, activating a tower, a Great
Fairy, freeing a Divine Beast, and more. What those milestones gave in the normal game (the Paraglider, the runes,
the champions' abilities, key armor, heart containers and stamina vessels) is shuffled into the multiworld instead,
and arrives in your game from wherever it was found.

The game runs on the Wii U version in the Cemu emulator. A game pack built for your seed replaces those rewards in the
game's own resources, and the Archipelago client delivers items while you play: see [In the game](ingame_en.md).

## Where are the options?

In the player's YAML file. The Archipelago Launcher writes a template with "Generate Template Options", and
[`BOTW.yaml`](https://github.com/EIdras/BOTW-Archipelago/blob/master/players/BOTW.yaml) is a ready one. Every option is explained [below](#options).

## Locations

| Locations | Count |
|---|---|
| Shrines (4 on the Great Plateau) | 120 |
| Sheikah Towers | 15 |
| Rune terminals of the Great Plateau | 4 |
| Great Fairy fountains | 4 |
| Divine Beasts, and their heart containers | 4 + 4 |
| Master Sword | 1 |
| Purah's rune upgrades, in Hateno | 3 |
| Songs of the Champions' Ballad | 4 |
| Beedle's shops (option) | 0 to 32 |
| Village stalls (option) | 0 to 28 |
| Chests: 1,180 on the surface, 174 in the shrines, 35 in the Divine Beasts (option `chest_sanity`) | 0 or 1,389 |
| Koroks (option `korok_sanity`) | 0 to 900 |
| Side quests (option `side_quest_sanity`) | 0 or 73 |
| Shrine quests (option `shrine_quest_sanity`) | 0 or 42 |
| Goddess Statue offerings (option [`spirit_orbs`](#spirit-orbs)) | 0, or 1 to 30 |
| Field bosses (option `boss_sanity`) | 0 or 86 |
| Master Mode chests (option `master_mode`, with `chest_sanity`) | 0 or 118 |

With `chest_sanity`, opening a chest sends its location's item. On `check_only`, the chest keeps its own contents,
and a window says what was found and for whom. On `ap_items`, a chest of the surface or of a Divine Beast holds the
item it sends, under its name, in place of its contents. A shrine's chest keeps its own unless `shrine_chest_items`:
a shrine's chest only changes with its whole shrine, so these shrines are built once from your own copy of the game,
then shared by every seed. That takes about 1 GB more, and the base game installed as a folder (not a `.wua` or
`.wud` file); without one, the shrines' chests keep their contents. A Divine Beast cannot be entered again once
freed: the chests left inside are sent then. The chests hold nothing needed to finish a game, unless
`chest_progression`: the logic then asks what opening each one takes (runes, bombs, Death Mountain's heat, a Divine
Beast freed, the Gerudo Set in Gerudo Town, and every rune inside a shrine or a Divine Beast). A chest frozen in ice,
under a boulder, after a Lynel's fight or made by a side quest still holds nothing needed, and a buried one nothing
needed in the first half of the game.

The Koroks are many: by default, 95 % of those that are locations hold filler of your own world
(`korok_local_filler`), so that they don't flood the other players with filler. With
`korok_progression`, the others may hold items needed to finish a game, and the logic asks what each
Korok's puzzle takes (bombs, Magnesis, the Gerudo Set in Gerudo Town).

A quest is checked once it is finished, and still gives its reward, but for the pieces of set items:
Thunder Magnet's Rubber Helm and Lynel Safari's Zora Greaves, which the Rubber and Zora Sets bring. The
quests hold nothing needed to finish a game, unless `quest_progression`. A shrine quest asks what its shrine asks. A side quest asks what
it takes in the game: a rune, an armor set, a Divine Beast freed, the Camera (Purah's, in Hateno) and the maps of
the regions it goes through; My Hero asks for the Master Sword, which then becomes a progression item. With
`quest_progression`, Hylian Homeowner and A Gift for the Great Fairy (rupees), The Weapon Connoisseur (weapons), From
the Ground Up and the two Tarrey Town quests that follow it (long), Hunt for the Giant Horse and The Royal White
Stallion (two stamina wheels to tame the horse, or an Enduring elixir) still hold nothing needed. Left out of the side quests: Slated for
Upgrades (Purah's upgrades are locations already), A Gift from the Monks, The Statue's Bargain, and the
EX quests of The Master Trials.

A boss is checked at its first defeat: the 86 Hinoxes, Stalnoxes, Stone Taluses and Moldugas of Hyrule whose defeat
the game saves, named after the nearest place on the map ("Hickaly Woods - Stalnox"). A Blood Moon brings the boss
back; its location stays sent. The bosses hold nothing needed to finish a game, unless `boss_progression`: the logic
then asks for the boss's region and, on Death Mountain's burning slopes, the heat's protection, never a weapon.

With `master_mode` and `chest_sanity`, the 118 chests only Master Mode has (The Master Trials, DLC 1), each on the
platform of an Octorok balloon, are locations too ("Great Plateau - Master Mode Wooden Chest"), as `chest_sanity`
says. The seed is then played in a Master Mode save: in a Normal mode one, which has none of these chests, the client
stops before giving anything. Without the option, a seed plays in either mode; in Master Mode, these chests keep their
contents.

## Items

**Progression and key items**

- The **Paraglider**, and the four runes: Magnesis, Cryonis, **Progressive Remote Bomb** and **Progressive Stasis**
  (the first copy is the rune, the second its upgrade, Remote Bomb+ or Stasis+).
- The **Progressive Sheikah Sensor**: the Sheikah Sensor, then the Sheikah Sensor+. Purah's camera no longer comes
  with it.
- Armor: Warm Doublet, Snowquill Set, Flamebreaker Set, Desert Voe Set, Zora Set, Rubber Set, and the Gerudo Set,
  which lets Link into Gerudo Town. Goron City's armor shop no longer sells the Flamebreaker Set, nor Vilia the
  Gerudo Set.
- The four champions' abilities, progressive: the first copy is the ability, the second the upgraded power of the
  Champions' Ballad (shorter recharge).
- Progressive Climbing Gear and Progressive Stealth Set (three pieces each).
- 17 Heart Containers and 5 Stamina Vessels, or 88 more Spirit Orbs in their place ([`spirit_orbs`](#spirit-orbs)).
- The maps of the 14 regions (all but the Great Plateau's), with the [`tower_maps`](#region-maps) option.

**Useful items**

- The Master Sword, the Hylian Shield, the Champion's Tunic, the Ancient Bridle and Saddle, the Barbarian, Ancient
  and Radiant sets.
- Pouch upgrades: 4 for weapons, 3 for bows, 4 for shields. Each one is one of Hestu's, who offers one fewer.
- The Master Cycle Zero (The Champions' Ballad), the Travel Medallion and the Korok Mask (The Master Trials).
- Epona, registered at the stables. With [`progressive_horse`](#progressive-horse), four Progressive Horses take her
  place and the Master Cycle Zero's.
- With [`bonus_items`](#bonus-items), up to 38 bonus items: armor and, as filler, saddles and bridles.
- Spirit Orbs, Ancient Cores, Star Fragments and Fairies. The Koroks still give their seeds, as in the game, even
  when they are locations.

**Filler**

- Arrows (normal, fire, ice, shock, bomb, ancient), elixirs, gems and rupees.
- Weapons, bows and shields: 83 of the game's, from the soldiers' to the Lynels', elemental and ancient ones, a few
  jokes (a Soup Ladle, a Pot Lid) and, rarely, the amiibo's treasures (Biggoron's Sword, the Twilight Bow...).
- With [`extra_filler`](#extra-filler), what upgrades armor, hearty and mighty food, and 20 Bomb Arrows.
- [Traps](#traps), with the `trap_percentage` option.

## Goal

The `goal` option says what finishes your game:

| `goal` | Finished when |
|---|---|
| `ganon` (default) | Calamity Ganon is defeated |
| `divine_beasts` | the four Divine Beasts are freed |
| `shrines` | `goal_shrines` shrines are cleared (1 to 120, default 60) |

Whatever the goal, Ganon's sanctum stays [sealed](#the-sealed-sanctum) until its own requirements are met.

## Logic

The Great Plateau is the only region reachable at first: its terminals need nothing, each of its four shrines needs
its rune, and leaving it needs the Paraglider. Beyond, the logic asks only for what the game itself blocks:

- **Runes on the way to a shrine's monk** (its chests left out). Where the game offers two ways, either rune is
  enough (Maka Rah's spiked balls: Magnesis or Stasis), unless one way is clearly the game's own. An entrance
  blocked by cracked rocks asks for Remote Bomb. The Divine Beasts ask for all four runes.
- **The Flamebreaker Set** where Link catches fire: Death Mountain, Goron City and the canyon around it, and Tarrey
  Town's arrow stall, whose merchant comes through the Southern Mine. Cold and desert heat are crossed with food and
  elixirs, as in the game: no armor is required for them.
- **The Zora Set** up the waterfalls to Vah Ruta.
- **The Gerudo Set** for Gerudo Town, for Vah Naboris, whose quest goes through the town, and for the shrine quests
  given in the town.
- **Purah's upgrades** once her quest Locked Mementos is done, which Impa gives in Kakariko. Each also asks for
  three ancient parts that Guardians drop, which the logic leaves out, as it does food.
- **The Champions' Ballad** once the four Divine Beasts are freed; its trials on the Great Plateau want the four
  runes, and each song what the way to its champion's region asks.
- **A freed Divine Beast** for its heart container, and for the shrines whose quest opens after it.
- **13 hearts for the Master Sword**, as in the game: 10 Heart Containers, or 40 Spirit Orbs with
  [`spirit_orbs`](#spirit-orbs) on `vanilla_statues`.

Only what these rules name is progression. The champions' abilities, the other armor, the climbing gear and the
stamina vessels help without being required.

## Options

| Group | Option | Default | In short |
|---|---|---|---|
| Goal | [`goal`, `goal_shrines`](#goal) | `ganon`, 60 | What finishes your game |
| Sanctum | [`sanctum_divine_beasts`](#the-sealed-sanctum) | 2 | Divine Beasts freed before Ganon (0 to 4) |
| | [`sanctum_shrines`](#the-sealed-sanctum) | 0 | Shrines cleared before Ganon (0 to 120) |
| | [`sanctum_master_sword`](#the-sealed-sanctum) | true | The Master Sword before Ganon |
| | [`sanctum_runes`](#the-sealed-sanctum) | true | The four runes before Ganon |
| Shops | [`beedle_shop_items`](#shops-and-stalls) | 0 | Archipelago items at each of Beedle's 16 shops (0 to 2) |
| | [`stall_items`](#shops-and-stalls) | 0 | Archipelago items on the village stalls (0 to 28) |
| Weapons | [`weapon_order`](#weapon-order) | `smoothed` | Weaker weapons first, stronger later |
| Maps | [`tower_maps`](#region-maps) | `region_keys` | Region maps are items, and keys of the logic |
| | [`early_map`](#region-maps) | `gentle` | One map among the Great Plateau's first checks |
| | [`towers_need_maps`](#towers-need-maps) | false | A tower needs its region's map too |
| | [`region_lock`](#region-lock) | false | Regions open from the Great Plateau outward |
| | [`map_travel_points`](#map-travel-points) | false | A map received opens a travel point |
| Horses | [`progressive_horse`](#progressive-horse) | false | Four horses in turn, for Epona and the Master Cycle Zero |
| Master Cycle Zero | [`bike_anywhere`](#master-cycle-zero-anywhere) | false | The bike in the desert and on Death Mountain |
| Spirit Orbs | [`spirit_orbs`](#spirit-orbs) | `containers` | Hearts and stamina as items, or from the statues |
| | [`statue_offerings`](#spirit-orbs) | 5 | With `statue_checks`, the statues' offerings that are locations (1 to 30) |
| Chests | [`chest_sanity`](#locations) | `off` | Chests as locations: `check_only`, or `ap_items` that the chests hold |
| | [`chest_progression`](#locations) | false | Chests may hold items needed to finish a game |
| | [`shrine_chest_items`](#locations) | false | With `ap_items`, the shrines' chests hold them too (about 1 GB more) |
| | [`master_mode`](#locations) | false | The 118 chests of Master Mode too, played in a Master Mode save |
| Koroks | [`korok_sanity`](#locations) | false | Koroks as locations |
| | [`korok_count`](#locations) | 100 | How many of the 900 (1 to 900) |
| | [`korok_local_filler`](#locations) | 95 | Share, in percent, holding filler of your own world (0 to 100) |
| | [`korok_progression`](#locations) | false | Koroks may hold items needed to finish a game |
| Quests | [`side_quest_sanity`](#locations) | false | The 73 side quests as locations |
| | [`shrine_quest_sanity`](#locations) | false | The 42 shrine quests as locations |
| | [`quest_progression`](#locations) | false | Quests may hold items needed to finish a game |
| Bosses | [`boss_sanity`](#locations) | false | The 86 field bosses as locations, at their first defeat |
| | [`boss_progression`](#locations) | false | Bosses may hold items needed to finish a game |
| Bonus Items | [`bonus_items`](#bonus-items) | 0 | Share of the filler turned into armor, saddles and bridles |
| Filler | [`extra_filler`](#extra-filler) | false | Armor upgrade materials, food and 20 Bomb Arrows too |
| Traps | [`trap_percentage`, `trap_weights`](#traps) | 0 | Share of the filler turned into traps (0 to 100) |
| | `death_link` | false | [DeathLink](#deathlink) |

### The sealed sanctum

Hyrule Castle's sanctum, where Ganon waits, stays sealed until what the `sanctum_` options ask is met, whatever the
goal ([what you see](ingame_en.md#the-sealed-sanctum)). Each option asks for one thing; 0 or `false` asks for
nothing. Three levels, as the options' presets set them:

| Preset | Divine Beasts | Master Sword | Runes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Easy | 4 | yes | yes |
| Medium (default) | 2 | yes | yes |
| Hard | 0 | no | no (Ganon whenever Link likes, as in the game) |

### Shops and stalls

- `beedle_shop_items`: Beedle sells that many Archipelago items, listed first, at each of his 16 shops (the 15
  stables and Kara Kara Bazaar).
- `stall_items`: that many Archipelago items, as jewels, spread at random over the 14 village stalls, 2 at most on
  one.

Buying one checks its location ([what you see](ingame_en.md#shops-and-stalls)).

### Weapon order

`weapon_order` orders the weapons wherever they land in the multiworld, by the logic's spheres:

- `smoothed` (default): the weaker first, the stronger as the game goes on, the amiibo's treasures last;
- `loosely_smoothed`: the same order, with some chance: a weapon may come a level earlier or later, never a treasure
  among the first;
- `anywhere`: wherever the fill put them, a treasure or the Master Sword on the Great Plateau too.

With `smoothed` and `loosely_smoothed`, your Master Sword is never on your Great Plateau (another player's early
locations may still hold it). The jokes come anywhere. With the region maps as keys, each map opens a sphere of its own, and the weapons grow region
after region.

### Region maps

A tower reveals one area of the game's map; each location belongs to the region of the tower whose map shows it.
`tower_maps` makes these maps items:

| `tower_maps` | The 14 maps are items | The logic asks for them |
|---|---|---|
| `region_keys` (default) | yes | yes: a region's locations are in the logic once its map is received |
| `items` | yes | no |
| `vanilla` | no: each tower reveals its own map | no |

With the maps as items, climbing a tower still counts as its location and opens its travel point, but no longer
reveals the map: a map received does, with the game's own animation.

> [!TIP]
> Nothing is locked in the game: a location done without its map counts all the same, it was just out of logic.
> The trackers show it as possible but out of logic.

With `region_keys`, the Great Plateau and Calamity Ganon need no map, nor do the towers unless `towers_need_maps` or
`region_lock` is on. A location whose quest goes through
another region needs that region's map too: Tarrey Town's arrow stall (its quest starts in Hateno once Link owns the
house there, then recruits in Eldin, the Wasteland and Tabantha), Purah's upgrades (Impa, in Kakariko, sends Link to
her), Shoqa Tatone (its quest wants pictures of Central Hyrule's Guardians, taken with Purah's camera), Kah Yah (its
quest wants Purah's camera), Shae Katha and Tutsuwa Nima (their doors want a scale of Farosh or Dinraal, who fly only
once Link has met Impa), Kah Mael (reached from Akkala's cliffs) and Revali's Song (one of its trials is in
Ridgeland).

`early_map` places one map among the Great Plateau's first checks (its rune terminals and its tower), so that a region
opens besides the towers (or at all, with `towers_need_maps`) once Link leaves the Plateau:

- `gentle` (default): one of the regions the game leads to first (Dueling Peaks, Hateno, Lake or Faron);
- `any`: one of the 14;
- `none`: none early.

What each combination asks for, with `tower_maps: region_keys`:

| Options | A region's locations need its map | A tower needs its map | A region must border one in the logic | The game keeps Link out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| none of these | yes | no | no | no |
| `towers_need_maps` | yes | yes | no | no |
| `region_lock` | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| `region_lock` and `map_travel_points` | yes | yes | no: its travel point is warped to | yes |

### Towers need maps

`towers_need_maps` (with `tower_maps: region_keys` only) puts each tower behind its region's map, like the rest of its
region, in any order. Off, the towers need no map, so that the early game has room before the maps come in: with
`early_map: none`, only the Great Plateau is in the logic until a map comes. `region_lock` always has the towers need
their map.

### Region lock

`region_lock` (with `tower_maps: region_keys` only) opens the regions from the Great Plateau outward, as the game's
map cuts them: a region is in the logic once its map is received **and** it borders a region already in the logic.
The Great Plateau borders Central, Dueling Peaks, Lake and the Wasteland. The logic leaves out the few borders the
game offers no way across (the cliffs around the Gerudo Highlands, the climb from Ridgeland to Hebra).

A tower then needs its region's map too, Calamity Ganon needs Central, a quest through another region needs to reach
that region, and `early_map` draws only among the Great Plateau's neighbours. The client keeps Link out of the regions
not yet in the logic ([what you see](ingame_en.md#region-borders)). Universal Tracker and the PopTracker pack follow
this option, from the seed's own borders: a location whose regions are out of reach shows as out of logic.

### Map travel points

`map_travel_points` (with the maps as items) makes a map received also open the travel point of one shrine near
where its region begins, once Link has the Paraglider, so that he can warp there at once; the game shows the shrine's name as it opens. The shrine stays
a location, cleared as ever. With `region_lock`, a region is then in the logic once its map and the Paraglider are
received, whether or not it borders a region in the logic (its tower still needs it), and `early_map` draws as without
`region_lock`.

### Progressive Horse

With `progressive_horse`, Epona and the Master Cycle Zero leave the items for four Progressive Horses, given in
this order: the Giant Horse, the Royal White Stallion with the royal saddle and bridle, Epona, then the Master
Cycle Zero. Each horse waits at the stables, as Epona does; with every stable full, it appears by Link. None is
needed to finish a game.

### Master Cycle Zero anywhere

The game refuses the Master Cycle Zero in the Gerudo Desert and on Death Mountain, and the invisible walls that stop
horses stop it too. With `bike_anywhere`, it can be summoned and ridden there and goes through those walls. Indoors
still refuse it, and flying onto the desert or Death Mountain from a cliff outside still throws Link off just before
landing. The logic does not change.

### Spirit Orbs

As in the game, any Goddess Statue (the Temple of Time's on the Great Plateau too) trades four Spirit Orbs for a heart
container or a stamina vessel, as you choose.

| `spirit_orbs` | Items | The Master Sword asks for |
|---|---|---|
| `containers` (default) | 17 Heart Containers, 5 Stamina Vessels, 20 Spirit Orbs | 10 Heart Containers |
| `vanilla_statues` | 108 Spirit Orbs: the statues give every heart and stamina vessel | 40 Spirit Orbs |
| `statue_checks` | 17 Heart Containers, 5 Stamina Vessels, four Spirit Orbs per offering | 10 Heart Containers |

With `vanilla_statues`, the logic counts on the statues' hearts: trading for stamina, or trading hearts back at the
Horned Statue in Hateno, keeps the Master Sword waiting. Only 40 orbs are needed; the others may lie anywhere, a Korok or
a chest that holds nothing needed too. The 66 more items need room: without it, generation stops and says so.
`chest_sanity`, or `korok_sanity` with a lower `korok_local_filler`, gives it.

With `statue_checks`, each trade at a statue is a location, "Goddess Statue - Offering 1" to the number
`statue_offerings` sets (5 by default, up to 30). The statue still takes the orbs and asks for a heart or stamina, then
gives nothing more: the offering sends its item, whatever you chose. Its scene shows the Archipelago item instead of
the heart or vessel, and so do the Divine Beasts' heart containers. Offering k asks for 4×k orbs, and the Temple of
Time's statue for a shrine cleared first, as in the game. Five offerings take the 20 orbs of `containers`; above some
ten, the orbs need locations that may hold progression: `korok_progression`, `chest_progression` or
`quest_progression` gives them.

### DeathLink

With `death_link`, Link's death kills the other DeathLink players of the room, with what killed him ("Player was slain
by a Bokoblin", "Player froze to death"...), and their deaths kill Link, as a lethal blow would: the death animation,
the Game Over screen and the reload of the last save. Mipha's Grace and fairies still save him; the received death is
then spent. It waits for a safe moment: not during a cutscene, a menu or a loading screen.

### Bonus Items

`bonus_items` turns that share of the filler (arrows, elixirs, weapons, gems and rupees) into bonus items, 38 at
most, none needed to finish a game:

- armor: the Sand and Snow Boots, the Thunder Helm, the Ruby, Sapphire and Diamond Circlets, the Topaz, Opal
  and Amber Earrings, the Bokoblin, Moblin, Lizalfos and Lynel Masks, the Hylian and Soldier's sets;
- the amiibo's sets: the Hero of Time, of the Wild, of the Sky, of Twilight and of the Wind;
- the DLC's armor: the Phantom, Tingle's, Fierce Deity and Royal Guard sets, Majora's Mask, Midna's and
  Zant's Helmets, Ravio's Hood;
- the Traveler's, Knight's, Royal, Monster and Extravagant saddles and bridles, for looks only: filler. A tamed
  horse wears them; Epona and the Giant Horse keep their own.

Traps keep their count: the bonus items take what they leave of the filler. The armor is useful, so it never
goes where nothing useful may: the chests, Koroks, quests and bosses whose `*_progression` option is off.

### Extra Filler

With `extra_filler`, the filler holds two more families, and 20 Bomb Arrows among the arrows:

- what upgrades armor at the Great Fairies: the scales, claws and shards of fangs and horns of Farosh, Dinraal
  and Naydra, the Lynels' horns, hooves and guts, the Guardians' screws, springs, gears and shafts, and
  Luminous Stones;
- hearty and mighty food: a Hearty Durian, a Big Hearty Truffle, Mighty Bananas, a Silent Princess, or a dish,
  Hearty Simmered Fruit, a Hearty Mushroom Skewer or Mighty Simmered Fruit.

The arrows, elixirs, weapons, gems and rupees come a little less often.

### Traps

`trap_percentage` turns that share of the filler (arrows, elixirs, weapons, gems and rupees) into traps, drawn by
`trap_weights` (a trap of weight 0 or left out never comes up). A trap strikes when it is received, at a safe moment.
Freeze, Lightning Strike and Fire are at 0 unless `trap_weights` gives them a weight.

| Trap | What it does |
|---|---|
| Weapon Shatter | The melee weapon in Link's hand is deleted. Empty hands, or the Master Sword: nothing. |
| Blood Moon | The Blood Moon rises at once and the defeated monsters come back. Where the game allows none, the next midnight is the Blood Moon instead. |
| Rupoor | Takes up to 100 rupees: the largest of 100, 50, 20, 10, 5 or 1 the purse holds. |
| Hearts Down | Takes up to two hearts, never the last quarter. |
| Strip Down | Link's weapon, shield, bow and armor go back in the pouch. |
| Cucco Swarm | The angry cuccos rush at Link from every side for 10 s. It can kill. |
| Yiga Ambush | Two Yiga Footsoldiers and a Yiga archer appear around Link and attack. |
| Paranoia | A Guardian takes aim at Link from behind, beeping, and vanishes just before it fires. |
| Downpour | Rain for 2 minutes (the walls get slippery), or a thunderstorm for 90 s (its lightning strikes metal). Nothing in a shrine; a death or a reload ends it. |
| Freeze | Link is frozen where he stands, and loses half a heart. |
| Lightning Strike | Calamity Ganon's lightning: a sign on the ground under Link, then the strike a second later. Three hearts and a shock if he is still there; he can run from it. |
| Fire | Link bursts into flames: a heart and a half, then more until he moves or reaches water. |

A trap given back after loading an older save is spent without effect: a trap is not suffered twice.

## Current limitations

- Only the Wii U version (European, American or Japanese), update v208, in Cemu on Windows or Linux (x86-64).
- A few mods are left out of the Archipelago game: see [Mods](mods_en.md#what-is-left-out).

tutorials.title: Multiworld Setup Guide
tutorials.description: Install the BOTW Archipelago release and play Breath of the Wild in Cemu in a multiworld.
tutorials.text:
# Breath of the Wild Multiworld Setup Guide

**Setup** · [In the game](ingame_en.md) · [Options](en_Breath%20of%20the%20Wild.md) · [Hosting](hosting_en.md) ·
[Trackers](poptracker_en.md) · [Mods](mods_en.md) · [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting_en.md)

This guide gets you from nothing to playing Breath of the Wild in an Archipelago room, on Windows or Linux, in Cemu.
Hosting the room is on [its own page](hosting_en.md).

## What you need

- [ ] Windows 10 or 11, or Linux on a 64-bit PC (x86-64): see [On Linux](#on-linux).
- [ ] [Archipelago](https://github.com/ArchipelagoMW/Archipelago/releases) 0.6.7 or newer.
- [ ] [Cemu](https://cemu.info/) 2.x.
- [ ] Breath of the Wild for **Wii U**, European (EUR), American (USA) or Japanese (JPN), from your own console, in
      Cemu's game list.
- [ ] Its **update v208** (1.5.0) and its **DLC**, installed in Cemu (File > Install game title, update or DLC).
- [ ] The game started once in Cemu.
- [ ] About 5 GB of free disk space, and 140 MB more for each seed. With `shrine_chest_items`, about 1 GB more,
      once for every seed, and the base game installed as a folder (not a `.wua` or `.wud` file).
- [ ] The link of the room's page, or your **slot file** (`.apbotw`): on the room's page, "Download Patch File..."
      next to your name.

> [!NOTE]
> The Switch version is not supported: the integration is built for the Wii U v208 executable. With several versions
> in Cemu, the launcher plays the European one, else the American one.

## Install

1. Install [Archipelago](https://github.com/ArchipelagoMW/Archipelago/releases) if you do not have it: the
   `Setup` program of its latest release (on Linux, its `AppImage`).
2. Download `botw.apworld` from the [releases](https://github.com/EIdras/BOTW-Archipelago/releases), in the
   release's **Assets**.
3. Open the **Archipelago Launcher**, click **Install APWorld** and choose `botw.apworld`. Close the Launcher and open
   it again.

<!-- ![BOTW Archipelago in the Archipelago Launcher](../../docs/images/ap-launcher.png) -->

That is all: BOTW Archipelago runs inside Archipelago. The host generates the seed with the same `botw.apworld`.

## Your first session

In the Archipelago Launcher, click **BOTW Archipelago**. The first time, it downloads the libraries it needs (about
14 MB, 18 MB on Linux, from the internet), then its window opens.

<!-- ![The first download](../../docs/images/setup-window.png) -->

<!-- ![The game found in your Cemu](../../docs/images/launcher-cemu.png) -->

1. **Cemu.** The first time, click **Choose Cemu...** and pick `Cemu.exe` (on Linux, Cemu's AppImage
   or the `Cemu` of its Linux zip). The launcher shows the game, its update
   and the DLC it found, and the room the profile takes. **Create the profile**: it copies Cemu and your saves into a
   profile of its own (about 5 GB). Your Cemu installation is never modified.
2. **The seed.** Click **Add from a room link...** and paste the link of the room's page
   (`https://archipelago.gg/room/...`): the launcher downloads your slot file from it, and asks which player you are
   when the room has several Breath of the Wild players. You can also click **Add a seed...** (Ctrl+O) and choose
   your slot file, or open it with **Open Patch** in the Archipelago Launcher. The launcher builds the
   seed's game pack, in about a minute. From a seed's zip, it asks which player you are.
3. **The room.** Its address (`archipelago.gg:38281`) is already filled in when your slot file comes from the room's
   page. Type the room's password if it has one, then click **Play**.

<!-- ![A seed added from its room's link](../../docs/images/launcher-room-link.png) -->

<!-- ![A seed ready to play](../../docs/images/launcher-seeds.png) -->

Cemu starts with the seed's game pack, and the window follows the session: the game pack, Cemu, the room, then your
save linked to the seed, with the checks found and the items received.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Start a new game** for a new seed: a save is bound to the seed it was started with.

Play normally: your items arrive in the game, and the Archipelago journal, top right of the screen, says what you
send and receive. [In the game](ingame_en.md) shows what to expect.

Close Cemu to end the session; the launcher's window can stay open. **Play again** starts the same seed in the same
room.

## The next sessions

Open **BOTW Archipelago** from the Archipelago Launcher again. The seeds already prepared are listed, the last played
first, with the version that generated them and the day they were last played. Pick one: its room is remembered.
Click **Play**.

To remove a seed you no longer play, select it and click **Delete...**: it deletes the seed and its game pack, and
keeps your saves.

## During a session

The session's log shows the room's messages in the colours of Archipelago's own client: your name in magenta, the
other players in pale yellow, locations in green, and items by kind (progression in purple, useful in blue, traps in
salmon, the others in cyan). **Search the log** highlights what you type in it; Enter goes to the place before,
Shift+Enter to the one after.

The line under the log goes to the room as chat. Archipelago's commands work too: `/hint <item>`, `/players`,
`/status`... are sent to the room as `!hint`, `!players`, `!status`.

<!-- ![A session's log](../../docs/images/launcher-session.png) -->

## Hints

The **Hints** page lists the room's hints for you: where your items are, and the items of other players in your
world, the ones still to find first. It shows only your items, or only your world, and hides the hints already found.
The last hints of a seed stay listed when no session runs.

During a session, once Cemu has started, it asks the room for a hint: choose an item of yours or a location of your
world, start typing its name and pick it in the list, then click **Ask for a hint**. A hint costs hint points, as in
the room's chat.

<!-- ![The Hints page](../../docs/images/launcher-hints.png) -->

## Updating

The launcher looks for a new release when it starts, and offers it at the top of its window: **Install** downloads
the new `botw.apworld` and puts it in place of yours (the previous one is kept in the data folder's `downloads`).
Then close Archipelago and open it again. **Settings** checks again, or turns the check off. Your profile, your seeds
and their saves are kept. The first time you play a seed with the new version, the launcher builds its game pack
again. Give the host the new `botw.apworld` for the next seeds.

Archipelago runs one version of a world at a time. A seed generated by a newer version is shown with **Update to
version X**. A seed generated by an older version that this one cannot play has to be generated again with this
one: the launcher says so.

The seeds of the versions before 0.4.0, when BOTW Archipelago was a program of its own, are shown with their version
in orange: **Play with version X** downloads that version next to this one and opens its own launcher (a console
window for the oldest). The versions installed this way are listed in **Storage**, where one you no longer need is
removed.

### Coming from version 0.3 or older

Install as above: the window finds your profile, your seeds and their saves where they are. The folder where you
unzipped the old release can then be deleted.

## On Linux

The same `botw.apworld` runs in Archipelago's Linux build, on a 64-bit PC (x86-64) with a distribution recent enough
for Archipelago's AppImage. Two differences from Windows:

- **Archipelago** comes as an AppImage: download `Archipelago_<version>_linux-x86_64.AppImage` from its
  [latest release](https://github.com/ArchipelagoMW/Archipelago/releases), make it executable
  (`chmod +x Archipelago_*.AppImage`) and open it.
- **Cemu**: its official AppImage, or the `Cemu` of its Linux zip, from [cemu.info](https://cemu.info/). Not a
  Flatpak or Snap Cemu: its sandbox hides Cemu from the client, so the launcher refuses it.

Nothing else to set up. Cemu very slow, or a session that cannot reach it: see
[Troubleshooting](troubleshooting_en.md#common-problems).

## Where things are

Your profile, your seeds, their game packs and the older versions installed are in the data folder:
`%LOCALAPPDATA%\BOTW Archipelago` on Windows, `~/.local/share/BOTW Archipelago` on Linux. **Storage** shows what
takes room in it, and moves it to another folder or drive. The libraries downloaded the first time are in
Archipelago's cache: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Archipelago\Cache\botw` on Windows, `~/.cache/Archipelago/botw` on Linux.

## Uninstalling

Delete `botw.apworld` from Archipelago's `custom_worlds` folder (on Linux, `~/.local/share/Archipelago/worlds`),
then the data folder (**Storage** shows where it is): the profile, with the saves of your Archipelago games, and the
seeds. Archipelago's cache folder named above can go too. Your Cemu installation was never modified.

---

Next: [In the game](ingame_en.md). Something went wrong? [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting_en.md). These guides are
also in the launcher: **Help**, at the bottom of its window's sidebar.
Running from the source code instead of a release:
[development](https://github.com/EIdras/BOTW-Archipelago/blob/master/docs/development.md#running-from-source).

tutorials.text:
# Breath of the Wild dans Archipelago : démarrage rapide

Ce guide court permet de jouer à Breath of the Wild dans une partie Archipelago, sous Windows ou Linux, dans
l'émulateur Cemu. Le reste de la documentation est en anglais : chaque section renvoie à sa page.

## Ce qu'il faut

- Windows 10 ou 11, ou Linux sur un PC 64 bits (x86-64, voir [Sous Linux](#sous-linux)), et
  [Cemu](https://cemu.info/) 2.x.
- Breath of the Wild **Wii U**, version européenne, américaine ou japonaise, depuis votre propre console, avec sa
  **mise à jour v208** et le **DLC** installés dans Cemu (Fichier > Installer un titre, une mise à jour ou un DLC).
  Lancez le jeu une fois dans Cemu. La version Switch n'est pas prise en charge.
- Environ 5 Go d'espace disque libre, et 140 Mo de plus par seed. Avec `shrine_chest_items`, environ 1 Go de plus,
  une seule fois pour toutes les seeds, et le jeu de base installé en dossier (pas en fichier `.wua` ou `.wud`).
- [Archipelago](https://github.com/ArchipelagoMW/Archipelago/releases) 0.6.7 ou plus récent.
- Le lien de la page de la salle, ou votre **fichier de slot** (`.apbotw`) : sur la page de la salle,
  « Download Patch File... » à côté de votre nom.

## Installer

1. Installer [Archipelago](https://github.com/ArchipelagoMW/Archipelago/releases) 0.6.7 ou plus récent, si ce
   n'est pas déjà fait : le programme `Setup` de sa dernière release (sous Linux, son `AppImage`).
2. Télécharger `botw.apworld` dans les [releases](https://github.com/EIdras/BOTW-Archipelago/releases), parmi les
   **Assets**.
3. Ouvrir l'**Archipelago Launcher**, cliquer sur **Install APWorld** et choisir `botw.apworld`. Fermer le Launcher
   et le rouvrir.

BOTW Archipelago tourne dans Archipelago : rien d'autre à installer. L'hôte génère la seed avec le même
`botw.apworld`.

## Jouer

Dans l'Archipelago Launcher, cliquer sur **BOTW Archipelago**. La première fois, il télécharge les bibliothèques
dont il a besoin (environ 14 Mo, 18 Mo sous Linux, depuis internet), puis sa fenêtre s'ouvre.

1. **Cemu** : la première fois, **Choose Cemu...** demande où est `Cemu.exe` (sous Linux, l'AppImage de
   Cemu ou le `Cemu` de son zip Linux), puis **Create the profile** copie
   Cemu et vos sauvegardes dans un profil à lui (environ 5 Go). Votre installation de Cemu n'est jamais modifiée.
2. **La seed** : **Add from a room link...**, puis coller le lien de la page de la salle
   (`https://archipelago.gg/room/...`) : le lanceur y télécharge votre fichier de slot. Ou bien **Add a seed...**
   (Ctrl+O) et choisir le fichier de slot, ou l'ouvrir avec **Open Patch** dans l'Archipelago Launcher. Son pack
   de jeu se construit en une minute environ.
3. **La salle** : son adresse (`archipelago.gg:38281`) est déjà remplie quand le fichier de slot vient de sa page.
   Taper le mot de passe de la salle s'il y en a un, puis **Play**.

Cemu démarre, et la fenêtre suit la session : les objets envoyés et reçus, en couleurs comme dans le client
d'Archipelago, le chat de la salle et ses commandes (`/hint <objet>`). La page **Hints** liste les indices de la
salle et en demande pendant une session. **Commencez une nouvelle partie** pour une nouvelle seed : une sauvegarde
reste liée à sa seed. Fermer Cemu termine la session ; **Play again** la relance.

Le lanceur propose lui-même les nouvelles versions : **Install** remplace votre `botw.apworld`, puis il faut
fermer et rouvrir Archipelago. Une seed d'avant la version 0.4.0 s'ouvre avec **Play with version X**, qui
télécharge sa version. En venant de la version 0.3 ou plus ancienne, le lanceur retrouve votre profil, vos seeds et
vos sauvegardes : le dossier de l'ancienne release peut être supprimé. Le guide complet, en anglais :
[Setup guide](setup_en.md). Les guides sont aussi dans le lanceur : **Help**, en bas de sa barre latérale.

## Sous Linux

Le même `botw.apworld` tourne dans la version Linux d'Archipelago, sur un PC 64 bits (x86-64) avec une distribution
assez récente pour l'AppImage d'Archipelago. Deux différences avec Windows :

- **Archipelago** est une AppImage : la télécharger dans sa dernière release, la rendre exécutable
  (`chmod +x Archipelago_*.AppImage`) et l'ouvrir.
- **Cemu** : son AppImage officielle, ou le `Cemu` de son zip Linux. Pas le Cemu Flatpak ni Snap : leur bac à sable
  cache Cemu au client, et le lanceur les refuse.

Rien d'autre à régler. Cemu très lent, ou une session qui ne l'atteint pas :
[Troubleshooting](troubleshooting_en.md#common-problems).

## Pour aller plus loin

| Je veux… | Page (en anglais) |
|---|---|
| Voir ce qu'Archipelago change dans le jeu | [In the game](ingame_en.md) |
| Comprendre les lieux, les objets, la logique et les options | [Options](en_Breath%20of%20the%20Wild.md) |
| Héberger une seed | [Hosting](hosting_en.md) |
| Suivre ma partie sur une carte | [Trackers](poptracker_en.md) |
| Jouer avec mes mods et packs graphiques | [Mods](mods_en.md) |
| Résoudre un problème, signaler un bug | [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting_en.md) |

## Noms en français

Archipelago et les textes ajoutés au jeu sont en anglais, et le jeu en français nomme souvent autrement les lieux et
les objets (Tah Muhl Shrine est le sanctuaire de Ta'Mur) : la [table des noms en français](names_fr.md) donne la
correspondance.

readme.text:
# Breath of the Wild for Archipelago

An [Archipelago](https://archipelago.gg) integration of **The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild**, Wii U version,
played in the [Cemu](https://cemu.info/) emulator.

<!-- ![An Archipelago item, received in Breath of the Wild](docs/images/item-received.jpg) -->

Shrines, towers, Great Fairies and Divine Beasts become checks of the multiworld, and, as you choose, chests,
Koroks, quests and field bosses too. The Paraglider, the runes, the
champions' abilities, armor and heart containers are shuffled across every game, and arrive in yours while you play,
presented by the game itself.

**Status: in testing.** Solo seeds and multiworlds with other games, hosted on archipelago.gg or on your own server.

## Highlights

- **Up to 2,857 locations**: the 120 shrines, the 15 towers, the Great Fairies, the Divine Beasts, the Master Sword,
  Purah's rune upgrades, the Champions' Ballad and, optionally, Beedle's shops, the village stalls, the chests (Master
  Mode's too), the Koroks, the side and shrine quests, the Goddess Statues' offerings and the field bosses.
- **Delivered by the game**: the item window, the Sheikah Slate's rune download, the champions' ability windows, the
  chests themselves. Each item is given once per save, through reloads and disconnections.
- **An Archipelago journal in the game**: items sent and received, hints, all in the game's own tip frame.
- **Region maps as keys**, and optionally a world that opens region by region from the Great Plateau.
- **A sealed sanctum**: Ganon waits until the seed's requirements are met.
- **DeathLink and twelve traps**, from a Blood Moon to a Yiga ambush or a lightning strike.
- **Horses given in turn**, armor and materials among the items, as you choose.
- **Trackers**: a PopTracker map pack built from your game, with the Koroks, chests and quests, and Universal
  Tracker; both show Link on the map.
- **A launcher inside Archipelago**: a seed added from its room's link, your Cemu never modified, the room's
  messages and your hints in its window, the PopTracker pack built for you, updates in one click
  ([Setup guide](botw_world/docs/setup_en.md)).
- **Your mods keep working**: FPS++, graphics packs, UKMM mods.

## What you need

- Windows, or Linux on a 64-bit PC, and [Cemu](https://cemu.info/) 2.x (on Linux, its AppImage or its Linux zip:
  see [On Linux](botw_world/docs/setup_en.md#on-linux)).
- Breath of the Wild for **Wii U** (European, American or Japanese), with **update v208 and the DLC**, from your own
  console. The Switch version is not supported.
- [Archipelago](https://github.com/ArchipelagoMW/Archipelago/releases) 0.6.7 or newer, to play and to generate.

No game file is part of this project: the game pack of a seed is built from your own copy of the game.

## Quick start

1. Download `botw.apworld` from the [latest release](https://github.com/EIdras/BOTW-Archipelago/releases), and
   install it with **Install APWorld** in the Archipelago Launcher.
2. In the Archipelago Launcher, open **BOTW Archipelago**, and add your seed from the link of its room's page.
3. Its window finds your Cemu, builds your seed's game pack, connects to the room and starts the game. It installs
   the updates too, lists the room's hints, and holds these guides (Help).

## Documentation

| I want to… | Read |
|---|---|
| Install and play | [Setup guide](botw_world/docs/setup_en.md) ([démarrage rapide en français](botw_world/docs/setup_fr.md)) |
| See what Archipelago changes in the game | [In the game](botw_world/docs/ingame_en.md) |
| Understand the locations, items, logic and options | [Game page and options](botw_world/docs/en_Breath%20of%20the%20Wild.md) |
| Host a seed | [Hosting](botw_world/docs/hosting_en.md) |
| Follow my game on a map | [Trackers](botw_world/docs/poptracker_en.md) |
| Play with my mods and graphic packs | [Mods](botw_world/docs/mods_en.md) |
| Fix a problem or report a bug | [Troubleshooting](botw_world/docs/troubleshooting_en.md) |
| Read the French names of locations and items | [Noms en français](botw_world/docs/names_fr.md) |

## Limitations

- Wii U version only, update v208, in Cemu on Windows or Linux (x86-64; not a Flatpak or Snap Cemu).
- The texts the integration adds to the game are in English.
- A seed is generated with Archipelago on a computer (archipelago.gg's website cannot generate it), then hosted
  anywhere, archipelago.gg included.
- A few mods cannot run with it: see [Mods](botw_world/docs/mods_en.md).

## Contributing

- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md): the world, the game pack, the client and how they work together.
- [Development](docs/development.md): running from source, layout, tests, reproducible builds, releases.
- [Technical notes](docs/reference/README.md): what was measured in the game, and why.

## Credits

- [Archipelago](https://github.com/ArchipelagoMW/Archipelago), the multiworld randomizer this integrates with.
- [oead](https://github.com/zeldamods/oead), [evfl](https://github.com/zeldamods/evfl) and
  [rstb](https://github.com/zeldamods/rstb) by leoetlino and the zeldamods community, for BOTW's file formats.
- [botw-tools](https://github.com/MrCheeze/botw-tools) by MrCheeze, whose GameData flag list served to map the locations.
- The [zeldaret/botw](https://github.com/zeldaret/botw) decompilation, as a reference for the engine.
- [Zelda Wiki](https://zeldawiki.wiki/), whose shrine and quest walkthroughs served to check the logic of every
  location.
- [Switch Toolbox](https://github.com/KillzXGaming/Switch-Toolbox), used to author the Archipelago item's 3D model.

## License

This project is free software, under the [GNU General Public License, version 3 or later](LICENSE): you may use, study,
share and modify it, and any version you distribute stays under the same license, with its source.

The license covers the project's own work. The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and its assets are © Nintendo; this
project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo. The icons attached to the `tracker-icons` release, which the
launcher downloads for the PopTracker pack, are Nintendo's images: they are not part of the repository and not under
its license.

notes.text:
## What's new in 0.4.0

The biggest update so far: up to **2,857 locations** (chests, Koroks, quests, Goddess Statues, bosses), the launcher
now **inside the apworld**, **Linux** support, new items and traps, and trackers that show it all.
Every new option is **off by default**: a YAML from 0.3 generates the same kind of seed as before.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **The release is now one file: `botw.apworld`.** No more zip to unzip: install `botw.apworld` with **Install
> APWorld** in the Archipelago Launcher, then click **BOTW Archipelago** there. Your profile, seeds and saves are
> found where they are. Seeds generated with 0.3 or older show their version: **Play with version X** opens them with
> that version. See [Updating](#updating).

> [!WARNING]
> **The logic of everything added in 0.4.0 is new, and certainly imperfect.** With thousands of new locations, some
> will ask for less, or more, than the game does. If a location is out of logic, unreachable, or a seed gets stuck,
> **please report it** (Discord or a GitHub issue) with the location's name and your seed: it will be fixed.

### A new launcher, inside Archipelago
The console launcher is replaced by a window of the apworld, opened from the Archipelago Launcher.
- **Installing `botw.apworld` is the whole setup.** The first time, the window downloads the libraries it needs
  (~15 MB ). The release zip is gone, and the host generates with the same `botw.apworld` (Archipelago 0.6.7 or newer).
- **Seeds from a room's link.** Paste the link of the room's page: the launcher downloads your slot file, asks which
  player you are when the room has several, and fills in the room's address. A slot file or a seed's zip works too,
  as does **Open Patch** in the Archipelago Launcher.
- **Your seeds at a glance**: listed with the version that generated them and the day they were last played, each with
  its room remembered. **Delete...** removes a seed and its game pack.
- **The whole session in one window**: the game pack built, Cemu started, the room joined and your save bound, step by
  step. The room's messages show in the colours of Archipelago's own client, and **Search the log** finds any of
  them. The line under the log is the room's chat, with Archipelago's commands (`/hint`, `/players`...).
- **A Hints page**: where your items are and what others look for in your world, with filters. During a session,
  pick an item or a location by name and click **Ask for a hint**.
- **PopTracker, ready**: **Settings** builds the PopTracker pack from your own game, and each session rebuilds it
  when it is out of date.
- **Updates in one click**: a new release is offered at the top of the window, and **Install** puts it in place of
  your `botw.apworld`. A seed generated by a newer version offers its update.
- **Older seeds still play**: a seed of 0.3 or older shows its version in orange, and **Play with version X** opens it
  with that version, installed side by side.
- **Storage**: what takes room in the data folder (seeds, game packs, older versions), and a move of the whole folder
  to another drive.
- **Help**: the guides, inside the window.
- **Clearer messages**: a seed that cannot be prepared says why, and what to do, in plain words.

### Linux (experimental)
- **BOTW Archipelago runs on Linux** (64-bit x86-64): Archipelago's AppImage, and Cemu's AppImage or Linux zip
  (not Flatpak or Snap). The setup guide has an "On Linux" section, and Troubleshooting covers the Linux problems.
- It has been played through a real multiworld game on Linux, but **far less tested than Windows**: expect
  Linux-only bugs, and please report them.

### New locations (all optional, all off by default)

| Option | Locations |
|---|---|
| `chest_sanity` (`check_only` or `ap_items`) | 1,389 chests: 1,180 on the surface, 174 in the shrines, 35 in the Divine Beasts |
| `master_mode` (with `chest_sanity`) | the 118 Master Mode chests |
| `korok_sanity`, `korok_count` | 1 to 900 Koroks drawn (100 by default) |
| `side_quest_sanity` / `shrine_quest_sanity` | 73 side quests / 42 shrine quests |
| `spirit_orbs: statue_checks`, `statue_offerings` | 1 to 30 Goddess Statue offerings |
| `boss_sanity` | 86 field bosses: Hinoxes, Stalnoxes, Stone Taluses, Moldugas |

- **Chests**: on `check_only` a chest keeps its contents and a window says what was found and for whom; on
  `ap_items` it holds the Archipelago item instead. `shrine_chest_items` changes the shrines' chests too (about 1 GB
  more, once for every seed, and the base game installed as a folder). A Divine Beast's chests still inside are sent
  when it is freed. `master_mode` asks for a Master Mode save.
- **Koroks**: each still gives its seed. `korok_local_filler` (95 % by default) keeps most of their filler in your own
  world, so they don't flood the others. The logic reads what each puzzle takes (bombs, Magnesis, the Gerudo Set).
- **Quests**: checked when finished, and they still give their reward. Thunder Magnet and Lynel Safari no longer
  give a piece of the Rubber and Zora Sets, which are items of the pool.
- **Goddess Statues** (`spirit_orbs`): `containers` is the game as before; `vanilla_statues` puts Spirit Orbs in the
  pool in place of the heart containers and stamina vessels (the Master Sword then asks for 40 orbs);
  `statue_checks` makes each offering a location, and the statue shows the Archipelago item it gives.
- **Progression**: by default these locations hold nothing needed to finish a game. `chest_progression`,
  `korok_progression`, `quest_progression` and `boss_progression` let them hold progression. Errands the logic cannot
  judge (rupees, long rebuilds, the horses that need two stamina wheels) and puzzles behind ice or ivy never do.
- **`towers_need_maps`**: with `region_keys`, a tower needs its region's map like the rest of the region.

### New items and traps (all off by default)
- **`progressive_horse`**: four Progressive Horses: the Giant Horse, the Royal White Stallion, Epona, then the Master
  Cycle Zero.
- **`bonus_items`**: a share of the filler becomes 38 bonus items: armor, masks, the amiibo and DLC sets, saddles
  and bridles.
- **`extra_filler`**: dragon, Lynel and Guardian parts, Luminous Stones, hearty and mighty food, Bomb Arrows.
- **Three new traps**: **Freeze**, **Fire** and **Lightning Strike** (Calamity Ganon's bolt, which shows its sign
  first and can be dodged). Their weights in `trap_weights` are 0 by default.

### Trackers
- **PopTracker** shows the chests, Koroks, quests, offerings and bosses of your seed once connected, with a toggle button per
  kind of location; **Link** marks where Link stands and **Follow** frames each region he enters.
- **Universal Tracker** (0.3.8 or later) gets a **Map** tab drawn from the PopTracker pack, with Link's arrow.

### Fixes
- **A fast travel while items arrive no longer freezes the loading screen.** Items now wait for Link in the world.
- An item due during a fast travel or a shrine lift no longer arrives 30 s late.
- An announcement no longer blocks the item queue when the game stops being ready at the wrong moment.
- On a new PC or a new data folder, items already received come back quietly with one summary, not one window
  each.
- Every Spirit Orb received shows its window.
- A map received at the foot of a tower shows its own region, not the tower's.
- With `smoothed` or `loosely_smoothed` `weapon_order`, the Master Sword no longer lands on your own Great Plateau.
- A seed that cannot be prepared says why, and what to do, in plain words.
- Pack builds are faster.

### Updating
- **Players**: in the Archipelago Launcher, **Install APWorld** with the new `botw.apworld`, close and reopen it, then
  click **BOTW Archipelago**. Your profile, seeds and saves are kept; the folder of the old zip can be deleted. Seeds
  generated with 0.3 or older play with **Play with version X**, which downloads that version next to this one.
- **Hosts**: install the 0.4.0 `botw.apworld` to generate. A 0.3 YAML still works; the new options are in the
  [options page](botw_world/docs/en_Breath%20of%20the%20Wild.md).
